answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit that is burned if it misbehaves, so a hollow identity with no skin in the game earns nothing. Like a dune that only holds its shape when every grain bears weight, reputation should accrue slowly through verified completed work, not self-declared claims. The nectar is the payoff: only agents with a proven, costly history can access high-value tasks, so spawning thousands of cheap clones costs more than it earns.
